title: What prophets longed to see came to Mary alone

edition.locus: Vossius 1684 Opera omnia, Latin column, In annuntiationem Sermo I, printed p. 13, cols. B-C (PDF p. 37)

source_text: Plurimi sanctorum Patrum, Patriarcharum, et prophetarum desiderarunt eum videre, et coram spectatores fieri, et non potuerunt. Et alii quidem ex ipsis per visiones adumbratim in aenigmatibus conspexerunt: alii vero in columna nubis divinam vocem audierunt, et sanctorum Angelorum aspectibus potiti sunt: ad Mariam autem virginem solam sanctam, Gabriel Archangelus claro lumine venit, Ave gratia plena, ei adnuntians: et sic ipsa Verbum suscepit, et in tempore corporeae completionis, pretiosam Margaritam produxit.
pass_a_gloss: Very many (plurimi) of the holy Fathers, Patriarchs, and prophets desired (desiderarunt) to see Him, and to become onlookers (spectatores) face to face (coram), and were not able (non potuerunt). And some of them through visions (visiones) shadowily (adumbratim) in riddles (aenigmata) beheld (conspexerunt): others in the pillar of cloud (columna nubis) heard the divine voice (divina vox), and obtained (potiti sunt) sights (aspectus) of holy Angels: but to Mary the virgin alone holy, Gabriel the Archangel came with clear light (claro lumine), announcing (adnuntians) to her Hail full of grace: and thus she received (suscepit) the Word (Verbum), and in the time of bodily completion (corporea completio), brought forth (produxit) the precious Pearl (pretiosa margarita).

choices.issue: desiderarunt eum videre ... et non potuerunt
choices.choice: 'desiderarunt eum videre ... et non potuerunt' echoes Matthew 13:17 / Luke 10:24; cited.
'adumbratim in aenigmatibus' may recall Numbers 12:8 or 1 Corinthians 13:12; uncertain, not cited.
'Patrum' rendered lower-case 'fathers' (the Old Testament fathers, not God the Father).

pass_b_english: Many of the holy fathers, patriarchs, and prophets longed to see Him and to become eyewitnesses, and could not (Matthew 13:17; Luke 10:24). Some of them saw Him in visions, dimly and in riddles; others heard the divine voice in the pillar of cloud (Psalm 99:7) and were granted the sight of holy angels. But to Mary alone, the holy Virgin, the Archangel Gabriel came in clear light, announcing to her: Hail, full of grace (Luke 1:28). And so she received the Word, and in the time of bodily fulfilment she brought forth the precious Pearl.
notes: 'desiderarunt eum videre ... et non potuerunt' echoes Matthew 13:17 / Luke 10:24; cited. 'in columna nubis divinam vocem audierunt' matches the Vulgate of Psalm 98:7 ('in columna nubis loquebatur ad eos'), which is Psalm 99:7 in English Bibles; English numbering cited (compare Exodus 33:9). 'adumbratim in aenigmatibus' may recall Numbers 12:8 or 1 Corinthians 13:12; uncertain, not cited. 'Patrum' rendered lower-case 'fathers' (the Old Testament fathers, not God the Father). 'Pearl' capitalised as a title of Christ, continuing section 11. Margin variants 'al. in aenigmate' and 'al. Angelus' not adopted.
source_notes: PDF p. 37 = printed p. 13, cols. B-C. Margins: at 'aenigmatibus' 'al. in aenigmate'; at 'Archangelus' 'al. Angelus'. 'adnuntians' printed 'adnuncians' (normalised as in section 1). 'desiderarunt eum videre ... et non potuerunt' echoes Matthew 13:17 / Luke 10:24 (no marginal note).
